policy: Historical mechanisms are admitted only as precisely scoped mathematical lessons. Reputation, analogy and finite experiments carry no proof authority.

sources.title: A Computing Procedure for Quantification Theory
sources.lesson: Exact elimination is not enough; charge the cross-resolvent or equivalent interface representation created by the elimination.

sources.title: Graph-Based Algorithms for Boolean Function Manipulation
sources.author: Randal E. Bryant
sources.lesson: Canonical exact DAG operations can be polynomial in diagram size while the diagram can be exponentially large in the original variable count; order and residual-state count are charged resources.

sources.title: A Knowledge Compilation Map
sources.lesson: A target language must be evaluated separately for succinctness and the queries/transformations it supports in polynomial time.

sources.title: Extending the Knowledge Compilation Map: Closure Principles
sources.lesson: Closure properties are representation-language properties that must be coupled to spatial efficiency and query complexity.

sources.title: Existential Closures for Knowledge Compilation
sources.author: Pierre Marquis
sources.lesson: Existential closure can make forgetting structurally available, but it does not by itself prove polynomial compilation from arbitrary CNF or a globally polynomial iterated representation size.

sources.title: A Strongly Exponential Separation of DNNFs from CNF Formulas
sources.lesson: Polynomial-size CNF does not imply polynomial-size DNNF; failure of a fixed compiled language is a lane-specific barrier, not a universal SAT lower bound.
